summary: An Indologist and linguist, Constantin D. Georgian studied at the University of Bucharest, Sorbonne, EPHE, and Leipzig (Ph.D. under Curtius, Leskien, Hübschmann, and Brockhaus). He taught Sanskrit at Bucharest (1877–1879) and Romanian at Academie für moderne Philologie.

id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
summary: Working in history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology, Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney, was Professor of History at École Normale Supérieure around 1794–1795 and studied under Alexander Hamilton circa 1802–1803.

Active in Indology, linguistics, and Tibetology, Régamey studied at Warsaw (M.A., Ph.D. under Schayer) and Paris. He held teaching posts at Warsaw (1935–1939), Lausanne (1945–1977), and Fribourg (1944–1977), and was president of the Swiss Asia Society (1962–1971).

Constantine Borissoff works in linguistics and Indology. He earned a Diplom in Oriental Philology at Far Eastern Federal University, a Sanskrit certificate at SOAS, and an MA at Birkbeck, University of London.

Cora Du Bois studied at Barnard College (~1923–1927) and UC Berkeley (~1929–1932). She worked at Hunter College (~1939–1942), the Office of Strategic Services (~1942–1945), the Department of State (~1945–1950), and Harvard University (~1954–1969).

Vreede-de Stuers completed her education and Ph.D. at the University of Paris. She served as librarian at Paris, the Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences, and the University of Indonesia, later becoming Lecturer in Cultural Anthropology at Amsterdam (1969–1973).

Corinna May Lhoir, working in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, pursued doctoral studies at Ghent University and the University of Hamburg, where she served as Lehrbeauftragte and yoga studies program coordinator (attested 2026).

A specialist in Tibetology and history and archaeology, Corneille Jest studied at Paris Descartes University and under André Leroi-Gourhan (1972). He spent his career at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (~1957–1995).

Working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Cornelis Jan Kuiken completed his MA under Jaap den Hollander and earned his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under the supervision of Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Tiele studied at the University of Amsterdam and Remonstrant Seminary. He was a pastor in Rotterdam, professor at the Remonstrant Seminary (1873), Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden (1877–1901), and Gifford Lecturer at Edinburgh (1896).

id: P:Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden
summary: Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden was a scholar in the field of Indology who completed his Ph.D. at Utrecht University in 1954 under the supervision of Jan Gonda.
Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as a professor at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Cortland Dahl studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Courtney Bruntz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a professorship at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and serves as Core Faculty and professor at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Craig Jamieson is a specialist in Indology and Buddhist studies. He is a fellow of Queens' College and served at the University of Cambridge, including as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Craig Preston studied at the University of Virginia, where he was a student of Joe Bransford Wilson and studied under Jeffrey Hopkins from 1980 to 1981.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Pecchia earned her PhD at Sapienza (2003) and studied at Vienna under Steinkellner. She has worked as a researcher at IKGA and lecturer at the University of Vienna.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She served as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~2000–2012) and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2001–2015).

Csaba Dezső is an Indologist who completed master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1991–1997) and earned his PhD at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2002.

Csaba Kiss earned his D.Phil. at Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. An Indologist, he was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2019–2024) and a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).
